# wallix-bastion_config_x509_ocsp (Resource)

Provides a resource to configure the revocation check, with OCSP (Online Certificate Status
Protocol), of the certificates used for X509 authentication.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_config_x509_ocsp" "main" {
  ocsp_check             = true
  default_ocsp_responder = "http://ocsp.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ocsp_check` (Boolean)

### Optional

- `default_ocsp_responder` (String)
- `ocsp_proxy` (String)
- `override_ocsp_responder` (Boolean)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Usage Notes

### Singleton Configuration

There is only one OCSP configuration on the Bastion and the API has no delete endpoint for it.
Destroying the resource only removes it from the state: the check stays as configured, because
disabling it on destroy (or when the resource is removed from the configuration during a
refactoring) would silently weaken certificate validation. To disable the check, apply
`ocsp_check = false` before removing the resource.

### Unset Arguments

The resource manages the whole OCSP configuration: every argument is sent to the API on creation
and on each update, with its empty value when it isn't set. Removing an argument from the
configuration resets it on the Bastion.

Creating the resource on a Bastion whose OCSP configuration was set elsewhere, for example in the
GUI, erases the arguments the configuration doesn't set, and the plan doesn't show it. Import the
existing configuration first: the plan then shows every value that would change.

## Import

The OCSP configuration can be imported using any ID (it is always stored as `x509OCSPConfig` in
state, since the API doesn't provide one), e.g.

```shell
terraform import wallix-bastion_config_x509_ocsp.main x509OCSPConfig
```
